11.67bc1e721e:
<n>118:1</n> <n>(Aleph)</n> Beáti immaculáti in via: * qui ámbulant in lege Dómini.
<n>118:2</n> Beáti, qui scrutántur testimónia eius: * in toto corde exquírunt eum.
<n>118:3</n> Non enim qui operántur iniquitátem, * in viis eius ambulavérunt.
<n>118:4</n> Tu mandásti * mandáta tua custodíri nimis.
<n>118:5</n> Útinam dirigántur viæ meæ, * ad custodiéndas iustificatiónes tuas!
<n>118:6</n> Tunc non confúndar, * cum perspéxero in ómnibus mandátis tuis.
<n>118:7</n> Confitébor tibi in directióne cordis: * in eo quod dídici iudícia iustítiæ tuæ.
<n>118:8</n> Iustificatiónes tuas custódiam: * non me derelínquas usquequáque.
<n>118:9</n> <n>(Beth)</n> In quo córrigit adolescéntior viam suam? * In custodiéndo sermónes tuos.
<n>118:10</n> In toto corde meo exquisívi te: * ne repéllas me a mandátis tuis.
<n>118:11</n> In corde meo abscóndi elóquia tua: * ut non peccem tibi.
<n>118:12</n> Benedíctus es, Dómine: * doce me iustificatiónes tuas.
<n>118:13</n> In lábiis meis, * pronuntiávi ómnia iudícia oris tui.
<n>118:14</n> In via testimoniórum tuórum delectátus sum, * sicut in ómnibus divítiis.
<n>118:15</n> In mandátis tuis exercébor: * et considerábo vias tuas.
<n>118:16</n> In iustificatiónibus tuis meditábor: * non oblivíscar sermónes tuos.
11.2e76ea82c4:
<n>118:1</n> <n>(Aleph)</n> Blessed are the undefiled in the way, * who walk in the law of the Lord.
<n>118:2</n> Blessed are they that search his testimonies: * that seek him with their whole heart.
<n>118:3</n> For they that work iniquity, * have not walked in his ways.
<n>118:4</n> Thou hast commanded * thy commandments to be kept most diligently.
<n>118:5</n> O! that my ways may be directed * to keep thy justifications.
<n>118:6</n> Then shall I not be confounded, * when I shall look into all thy commandments.
<n>118:7</n> I will praise thee with uprightness of heart, * when I shall have learned the judgments of thy justice.
<n>118:8</n> I will keep thy justifications: * O! do not thou utterly forsake me.
<n>118:9</n> <n>(Béth)</n> By what doth a young man correct his way? * By observing thy words.
<n>118:10</n> With my whole heart have I sought after thee: * let me not stray from thy commandments.
<n>118:11</n> Thy words have I hidden in my heart, * that I may not sin against thee.
<n>118:12</n> Blessed art thou, O Lord: * teach me thy justifications.
<n>118:13</n> With my lips * I have pronounced all the judgments of thy mouth.
<n>118:14</n> I have been delighted in the way of thy testimonies, * as in all riches.
<n>118:15</n> I will meditate on thy commandments: * and I will consider thy ways.
<n>118:16</n> I will think of thy justifications: * I will not forget thy words.
11.8d7dfb064f:
<n>118:17</n> <n>(Ghimel)</n> Retríbue servo tuo, vivífica me: * et custódiam sermónes tuos:
<n>118:18</n> Revéla óculos meos: * et considerábo mirabília de lege tua.
<n>118:19</n> Íncola ego sum in terra: * non abscóndas a me mandáta tua.
<n>118:20</n> Concupívit ánima mea desideráre iustificatiónes tuas, * in omni témpore.
<n>118:21</n> Increpásti supérbos: * maledícti qui declínant a mandátis tuis.
<n>118:22</n> Aufer a me oppróbrium, et contémptum: * quia testimónia tua exquisívi.
<n>118:23</n> Étenim sedérunt príncipes, et advérsum me loquebántur: * servus autem tuus exercebátur in iustificatiónibus tuis.
<n>118:24</n> Nam et testimónia tua meditátio mea est: * et consílium meum iustificatiónes tuæ.
<n>118:25</n> <n>(Daleth)</n> Adhǽsit paviménto ánima mea: * vivífica me secúndum verbum tuum.
<n>118:26</n> Vias meas enuntiávi, et exaudísti me: * doce me iustificatiónes tuas.
<n>118:27</n> Viam iustificatiónum tuárum ínstrue me: * et exercébor in mirabílibus tuis.
<n>118:28</n> Dormitávit ánima mea præ tǽdio: * confírma me in verbis tuis.
<n>118:29</n> Viam iniquitátis ámove a me: * et de lege tua miserére mei.
<n>118:30</n> Viam veritátis elégi: * iudícia tua non sum oblítus.
<n>118:31</n> Adhǽsi testimóniis tuis, Dómine: * noli me confúndere.
<n>118:32</n> Viam mandatórum tuórum cucúrri, * cum dilatásti cor meum.
11.bf7c8ef58b:
<n>118:17</n> <n>(Ghimel)</n> Give bountifully to thy servant, enliven me * and I shall keep thy words.
<n>118:18</n> Open thou my eyes: * and I will consider the wondrous things of thy law.
<n>118:19</n> I am a sojourner on the earth: * hide not thy commandments from me.
<n>118:20</n> My soul hath coveted to long for thy justifications, * at all times.
<n>118:21</n> Thou hast rebuked the proud: * they are cursed who decline from thy commandments.
<n>118:22</n> Remove from me reproach and contempt: * because I have sought after thy testimonies.
<n>118:23</n> For princes sat, and spoke against me: * but thy servant was employed in thy justifications.
<n>118:24</n> For thy testimonies are my meditation: * and thy justifications my counsel.
<n>118:25</n> <n>(Daleth)</n> My soul hath cleaved to the pavement: * quicken thou me according to thy word.
<n>118:26</n> I have declared my ways, and thou hast heard me: * teach me thy justifications.
<n>118:27</n> Make me to understand the way of thy justifications: * and I shall be exercised in thy wondrous works.
<n>118:28</n> My soul hath slumbered through heaviness: * strengthen thou me in thy words.
<n>118:29</n> Remove from me the way of iniquity: * and out of thy law have mercy on me.
<n>118:30</n> I have chosen the way of truth: * thy judgments I have not forgotten.
<n>118:31</n> I have stuck to thy testimonies, O Lord: * put me not to shame.
<n>118:32</n> I have run the way of thy commandments, * when thou didst enlarge my heart.
11.66d6af014b:
<n>116:1</n> Laudáte Dóminum, omnes gentes: * laudáte eum, omnes pópuli:
<n>116:2</n> Quóniam confirmáta est super nos misericórdia eius: * et véritas Dómini manet in ætérnum.
11.0a67a14e81:
<n>116:1</n> O Praise the Lord, all ye nations: * praise him, all ye people.
<n>116:2</n> For his mercy is confirmed upon us: * and the truth of the Lord remaineth for ever.
11.bfac8827ba:
<n>118:33</n> <n>(He)</n> Legem pone mihi, Dómine, viam iustificatiónum tuárum: * et exquíram eam semper.
<n>118:34</n> Da mihi intelléctum, et scrutábor legem tuam: * et custódiam illam in toto corde meo.
<n>118:35</n> Deduc me in sémitam mandatórum tuórum: * quia ipsam vólui.
<n>118:36</n> Inclína cor meum in testimónia tua: * et non in avarítiam.
<n>118:37</n> Avérte óculos meos ne vídeant vanitátem: * in via tua vivífica me.
<n>118:38</n> Státue servo tuo elóquium tuum, * in timóre tuo.
<n>118:39</n> Ámputa oppróbrium meum quod suspicátus sum: * quia iudícia tua iucúnda.
<n>118:40</n> Ecce, concupívi mandáta tua: * in æquitáte tua vivífica me.
<n>118:41</n> <n>(Vav)</n> Et véniat super me misericórdia tua, Dómine: * salutáre tuum secúndum elóquium tuum.
<n>118:42</n> Et respondébo exprobrántibus mihi verbum: * quia sperávi in sermónibus tuis.
<n>118:43</n> Et ne áuferas de ore meo verbum veritátis usquequáque: * quia in iudíciis tuis supersperávi.
<n>118:44</n> Et custódiam legem tuam semper: * in sǽculum et in sǽculum sǽculi.
<n>118:45</n> Et ambulábam in latitúdine: * quia mandáta tua exquisívi.
<n>118:46</n> Et loquébar in testimóniis tuis in conspéctu regum: * et non confundébar.
<n>118:47</n> Et meditábar in mandátis tuis, * quæ diléxi.
<n>118:48</n> Et levávi manus meas ad mandáta tua, quæ diléxi: * et exercébar in iustificatiónibus tuis.
11.42dc21a471:
<n>118:33</n> <n>(He)</n> Set before me for a law the way of thy justifications, O Lord: * and I will always seek after it.
<n>118:34</n> Give me understanding, and I will search thy law; * and I will keep it with my whole heart.
<n>118:35</n> Lead me into the path of thy commandments; * for this same I have desired.
<n>118:36</n> Incline my heart into thy testimonies * and not to covetousness.
<n>118:37</n> Turn away my eyes that they may not behold vanity: * quicken me in thy way.
<n>118:38</n> Establish thy word to thy servant, * in thy fear.
<n>118:39</n> Turn away my reproach, which I have apprehended: * for thy judgments are delightful.
<n>118:40</n> Behold I have longed after thy precepts: * quicken me in thy justice.
<n>118:41</n> <n>(Vau)</n> Let thy mercy also come upon me, O Lord: * thy salvation according to thy word.
<n>118:42</n> So shall I answer them that reproach me in any thing; * that I have trusted in thy words.
<n>118:43</n> And take not thou the word of truth utterly out of my mouth: * for in thy words, I have hoped exceedingly.
<n>118:44</n> So shall I always keep thy law, * for ever and ever.
<n>118:45</n> And I walked at large: * because I have sought after thy commandments.
<n>118:46</n> And I spoke of thy testimonies before kings: * and I was not ashamed.
<n>118:47</n> I meditated also on thy commandments, * which I loved.
<n>118:48</n> And I lifted up my hands to thy commandments, which I loved: * and I was exercised in thy justifications.
11.06a201ad82:
<n>118:49</n> <n>(Zai)</n> Memor esto verbi tui servo tuo, * in quo mihi spem dedísti.
<n>118:50</n> Hæc me consoláta est in humilitáte mea: * quia elóquium tuum vivificávit me.
<n>118:51</n> Supérbi iníque agébant usquequáque: * a lege autem tua non declinávi.
<n>118:52</n> Memor fui iudiciórum tuórum a sǽculo, Dómine: * et consolátus sum.
<n>118:53</n> Deféctio ténuit me, * pro peccatóribus derelinquéntibus legem tuam.
<n>118:54</n> Cantábiles mihi erant iustificatiónes tuæ, * in loco peregrinatiónis meæ.
<n>118:55</n> Memor fui nocte nóminis tui, Dómine: * et custodívi legem tuam.
<n>118:56</n> Hæc facta est mihi: * quia iustificatiónes tuas exquisívi.
<n>118:57</n> <n>(Heth)</n> Pórtio mea, Dómine, * dixi custodíre legem tuam.
<n>118:58</n> Deprecátus sum fáciem tuam in toto corde meo: * miserére mei secúndum elóquium tuum.
<n>118:59</n> Cogitávi vias meas: * et convérti pedes meos in testimónia tua.
<n>118:60</n> Parátus sum, et non sum turbátus: * ut custódiam mandáta tua.
<n>118:61</n> Funes peccatórum circumpléxi sunt me: * et legem tuam non sum oblítus.
<n>118:62</n> Média nocte surgébam ad confiténdum tibi, * super iudícia iustificatiónis tuæ.
<n>118:63</n> Párticeps ego sum ómnium timéntium te: * et custodiéntium mandáta tua.
<n>118:64</n> Misericórdia tua, Dómine, plena est terra: * iustificatiónes tuas doce me.
11.aa9872cf11:
<n>118:49</n> <n>(Zai)</n> Be thou mindful of thy word to thy servant, * in which thou hast given me hope.
<n>118:50</n> This hath comforted me in my humiliation: * because thy word hath enlivened me.
<n>118:51</n> The proud did iniquitously altogether: * but I declined not from thy law.
<n>118:52</n> I remembered, O Lord, thy judgments of old: * and I was comforted.
<n>118:53</n> A fainting hath taken hold of me, * because of the wicked that forsake thy law.
<n>118:54</n> Thy justifications were the subject of my song, * in the place of my pilgrimage.
<n>118:55</n> In the night I have remembered thy name, O Lord: * and have kept thy law.
<n>118:56</n> This happened to me: * because I sought after thy justifications.
<n>118:57</n> <n>(Heth)</n> O Lord, my portion, * I have said, I would keep thy law.
<n>118:58</n> I entreated thy face with all my heart: * have mercy on me according to thy word.
<n>118:59</n> I have thought on my ways: * and turned my feet unto thy testimonies.
<n>118:60</n> I am ready, and am not troubled: * that I may keep thy commandments.
<n>118:61</n> The cords of the wicked have encompassed me: * but I have not forgotten thy law.
<n>118:62</n> I rose at midnight to give praise to thee; * for the judgments of thy justification.
<n>118:63</n> I am a partaker with all them that fear thee, * and that keep thy commandments.
<n>118:64</n> The earth, O Lord, is full of thy mercy: * teach me thy justifications.
11.d9507ca6ae:
<n>118:65</n> <n>(Teth)</n> Bonitátem fecísti cum servo tuo, Dómine, * secúndum verbum tuum.
<n>118:66</n> Bonitátem, et disciplínam, et sciéntiam doce me: * quia mandátis tuis crédidi.
<n>118:67</n> Priúsquam humiliárer ego delíqui: * proptérea elóquium tuum custodívi.
<n>118:68</n> Bonus es tu: * et in bonitáte tua doce me iustificatiónes tuas.
<n>118:69</n> Multiplicáta est super me iníquitas superbórum: * ego autem in toto corde meo scrutábor mandáta tua.
<n>118:70</n> Coagulátum est sicut lac cor eórum: * ego vero legem tuam meditátus sum.
<n>118:71</n> Bonum mihi quia humiliásti me: * ut discam iustificatiónes tuas.
<n>118:72</n> Bonum mihi lex oris tui, * super míllia auri et argénti.
<n>118:73</n> <n>(Ioth)</n> Manus tuæ fecérunt me, et plasmavérunt me: * da mihi intelléctum, et discam mandáta tua.
<n>118:74</n> Qui timent te vidébunt me, et lætabúntur: * quia in verba tua supersperávi.
<n>118:75</n> Cognóvi, Dómine, quia ǽquitas iudícia tua: * et in veritáte tua humiliásti me.
<n>118:76</n> Fiat misericórdia tua ut consolétur me, * secúndum elóquium tuum servo tuo.
<n>118:77</n> Véniant mihi miseratiónes tuæ, et vivam: * quia lex tua meditátio mea est.
<n>118:78</n> Confundántur supérbi, quia iniúste iniquitátem fecérunt in me: * ego autem exercébor in mandátis tuis.
<n>118:79</n> Convertántur mihi timéntes te: * et qui novérunt testimónia tua.
<n>118:80</n> Fiat cor meum immaculátum in iustificatiónibus tuis, * ut non confúndar.
11.181a6f1698:
<n>118:65</n> <n>(Teth)</n> Thou hast done well with thy servant, O Lord, * according to thy word.
<n>118:66</n> Teach me goodness and discipline and knowledge; * for I have believed thy commandments.
<n>118:67</n> Before I was humbled I offended; * therefore have I kept thy word.
<n>118:68</n> Thou art good; * and in thy goodness teach me thy justifications.
<n>118:69</n> The iniquity of the proud hath been multiplied over me: * but I will seek thy commandments with my whole heart.
<n>118:70</n> Their heart is curdled like milk: * but I have meditated on thy law.
<n>118:71</n> It is good for me that thou hast humbled me, * that I may learn thy justifications.
<n>118:72</n> The law of thy mouth is good to me, * above thousands of gold and silver.
<n>118:73</n> <n>(Jod)</n> Thy hands have made me and formed me: * give me understanding, and I will learn thy commandments.
<n>118:74</n> They that fear thee shall see me, and shall be glad: * because I have greatly hoped in thy words.
<n>118:75</n> I know, O Lord, that thy judgments are equity: * and in thy truth thou hast humbled me.
<n>118:76</n> O! let thy mercy be for my comfort, * according to thy word unto thy servant.
<n>118:77</n> Let thy tender mercies come unto me, and I shall live: * for thy law is my meditation.
<n>118:78</n> Let the proud be ashamed, because they have done unjustly towards me: * but I will be employed in thy commandments.
<n>118:79</n> Let them that fear thee turn to me: * and they that know thy testimonies.
<n>118:80</n> Let my heart be undefiled in thy justifications, * that I may not be confounded.
11.746598834b:
<n>118:81</n> <n>(Caph)</n> Defécit in salutáre tuum ánima mea: * et in verbum tuum supersperávi.
<n>118:82</n> Defecérunt óculi mei in elóquium tuum, * dicéntes: Quando consoláberis me?
<n>118:83</n> Quia factus sum sicut uter in pruína: * iustificatiónes tuas non sum oblítus.
<n>118:84</n> Quot sunt dies servi tui? * quando fácies de persequéntibus me iudícium?
<n>118:85</n> Narravérunt mihi iníqui fabulatiónes: * sed non ut lex tua.
<n>118:86</n> Ómnia mandáta tua véritas: * iníque persecúti sunt me, ádiuva me.
<n>118:87</n> Paulo minus consummavérunt me in terra: * ego autem non derelíqui mandáta tua.
<n>118:88</n> Secúndum misericórdiam tuam vivífica me: * et custódiam testimónia oris tui.
<n>118:89</n> <n>(Lamed)</n> In ætérnum, Dómine, * verbum tuum pérmanet in cælo.
<n>118:90</n> In generatiónem et generatiónem véritas tua: * fundásti terram, et pérmanet.
<n>118:91</n> Ordinatióne tua persevérat dies: * quóniam ómnia sérviunt tibi.
<n>118:92</n> Nisi quod lex tua meditátio mea est: * tunc forte periíssem in humilitáte mea.
<n>118:93</n> In ætérnum non oblivíscar iustificatiónes tuas: * quia in ipsis vivificásti me.
<n>118:94</n> Tuus sum ego, salvum me fac: * quóniam iustificatiónes tuas exquisívi.
<n>118:95</n> Me exspectavérunt peccatóres ut pérderent me: * testimónia tua intelléxi.
<n>118:96</n> Omnis consummatiónis vidi finem: * latum mandátum tuum nimis.
11.ae43aced4f:
<n>118:81</n> <n>(Caph)</n> My soul hath fainted after thy salvation: * and in thy word I have very much hoped.
<n>118:82</n> My eyes have failed for thy word, * saying: When wilt thou comfort me?
<n>118:83</n> For I am become like a bottle in the frost: * I have not forgotten thy justifications.
<n>118:84</n> How many are the days of thy servant: * when wilt thou execute judgment on them that persecute me?
<n>118:85</n> The wicked have told me fables: * but not as thy law.
<n>118:86</n> All thy statutes are truth: * they have persecuted me unjustly, do thou help me.
<n>118:87</n> They had almost made an end of me upon earth: * but I have not forsaken thy commandments.
<n>118:88</n> Quicken thou me according to thy mercy: * and I shall keep the testimonies of thy mouth.
<n>118:89</n> <n>(Lamed)</n> For ever, O Lord, * thy word standeth firm in heaven.
<n>118:90</n> Thy truth unto all generations: * thou hast founded the earth, and it continueth.
<n>118:91</n> By thy ordinance the day goeth on: * for all things serve thee.
<n>118:92</n> Unless thy law had been my meditation, * I had then perhaps perished in my abjection.
<n>118:93</n> Thy justifications I will never forget: * for by them thou hast given me life.
<n>118:94</n> I am thine, save thou me: * for I have sought thy justifications.
<n>118:95</n> The wicked have waited for me to destroy me: * but I have understood thy testimonies.
<n>118:96</n> I have seen an end of all perfection: * thy commandment is exceeding broad.
11.871eebfad0:
<n>118:97</n> <n>(Mem)</n> Quómodo diléxi legem tuam, Dómine? * tota die meditátio mea est.
<n>118:98</n> Super inimícos meos prudéntem me fecísti mandáto tuo: * quia in ætérnum mihi est.
<n>118:99</n> Super omnes docéntes me intelléxi: * quia testimónia tua meditátio mea est.
<n>118:100</n> Super senes intelléxi: * quia mandáta tua quæsívi.
<n>118:101</n> Ab omni via mala prohíbui pedes meos: * ut custódiam verba tua.
<n>118:102</n> A iudíciis tuis non declinávi: * quia tu legem posuísti mihi.
<n>118:103</n> Quam dúlcia fáucibus meis elóquia tua, * super mel ori meo!
<n>118:104</n> A mandátis tuis intelléxi: * proptérea odívi omnem viam iniquitátis.
<n>118:105</n> <n>(Nun)</n> Lucérna pédibus meis verbum tuum, * et lumen sémitis meis.
<n>118:106</n> Iurávi, et státui * custodíre iudícia iustítiæ tuæ.
<n>118:107</n> Humiliátus sum usquequáque, Dómine: * vivífica me secúndum verbum tuum.
<n>118:108</n> Voluntária oris mei beneplácita fac, Dómine: * et iudícia tua doce me.
<n>118:109</n> Ánima mea in mánibus meis semper: * et legem tuam non sum oblítus.
<n>118:110</n> Posuérunt peccatóres láqueum mihi: * et de mandátis tuis non errávi.
<n>118:111</n> Hereditáte acquisívi testimónia tua in ætérnum: * quia exsultátio cordis mei sunt.
<n>118:112</n> Inclinávi cor meum ad faciéndas iustificatiónes tuas in ætérnum, * propter retributiónem.
11.3d66fdba5b:
<n>118:97</n> <n>(Mem)</n> How have I loved thy law, O Lord! * it is my meditation all the day.
<n>118:98</n> Through thy commandment, thou hast made me wiser than my enemies: * for it is ever with me.
<n>118:99</n> I have understood more than all my teachers: * because thy testimonies are my meditation.
<n>118:100</n> I have had understanding above ancients: * because I have sought thy commandments.
<n>118:101</n> I have restrained my feet from every evil way: * that I may keep thy words.
<n>118:102</n> I have not declined from thy judgments, * because thou hast set me a law.
<n>118:103</n> How sweet are thy words to my palate! * more than honey to my mouth.
<n>118:104</n> By thy commandments I have had understanding: * therefore have I hated every way of iniquity.
<n>118:105</n> <n>(Nun)</n> Thy word is a lamp to my feet, * and a light to my paths.
<n>118:106</n> I have sworn and am determined * to keep the judgments of thy justice.
<n>118:107</n> I have been humbled, O Lord, exceedingly: * quicken thou me according to thy word.
<n>118:108</n> The free offerings of my mouth make acceptable, O Lord: * and teach me thy judgments.
<n>118:109</n> My soul is continually in my hands: * and I have not forgotten thy law.
<n>118:110</n> Sinners have laid a snare for me: * but I have not erred from thy precepts.
<n>118:111</n> I have purchased thy testimonies for an inheritance for ever: * because they are the joy of my heart.
<n>118:112</n> I have inclined my heart to do thy justifications for ever, * for the reward.
11.da964c7117:
<n>118:113</n> <n>(Samech)</n> Iníquos ódio hábui: * et legem tuam diléxi.
<n>118:114</n> Adiútor et suscéptor meus es tu: * et in verbum tuum supersperávi.
<n>118:115</n> Declináte a me, malígni: * et scrutábor mandáta Dei mei.
<n>118:116</n> Súscipe me secúndum elóquium tuum, et vivam: * et non confúndas me ab exspectatióne mea.
<n>118:117</n> Ádiuva me, et salvus ero: * et meditábor in iustificatiónibus tuis semper.
<n>118:118</n> Sprevísti omnes discedéntes a iudíciis tuis: * quia iniústa cogitátio eórum.
<n>118:119</n> Prævaricántes reputávi omnes peccatóres terræ: * ídeo diléxi testimónia tua.
<n>118:120</n> Confíge timóre tuo carnes meas: * a iudíciis enim tuis tímui.
<n>118:121</n> <n>(Ain)</n> Feci iudícium et iustítiam: * non tradas me calumniántibus me.
<n>118:122</n> Súscipe servum tuum in bonum: * non calumniéntur me supérbi.
<n>118:123</n> Óculi mei defecérunt in salutáre tuum: * et in elóquium iustítiæ tuæ.
<n>118:124</n> Fac cum servo tuo secúndum misericórdiam tuam: * et iustificatiónes tuas doce me.
<n>118:125</n> Servus tuus sum ego: * da mihi intelléctum, ut sciam testimónia tua.
<n>118:126</n> Tempus faciéndi, Dómine: * dissipavérunt legem tuam.
<n>118:127</n> Ídeo diléxi mandáta tua, * super aurum et topázion.
<n>118:128</n> Proptérea ad ómnia mandáta tua dirigébar: * omnem viam iníquam ódio hábui.
11.b499fc92cb:
<n>118:113</n> <n>(Samech)</n> I have hated the unjust: * and I have loved thy law.
<n>118:114</n> Thou art my helper and my protector: * and in thy word I have greatly hoped.
<n>118:115</n> Depart from me, ye malignant: * and I will search the commandments of my God.
<n>118:116</n> Uphold me according to thy word, and I shall live: * and let me not be confounded in my expectation.
<n>118:117</n> Help me, and I shall be saved: * and I will meditate always on thy justifications.
<n>118:118</n> Thou hast despised all them that fall off from thy judgments; * for their thought is unjust.
<n>118:119</n> I have accounted all the sinners of the earth prevaricators: * therefore have I loved thy testimonies.
<n>118:120</n> Pierce thou my flesh with thy fear: * for I am afraid of thy judgments.
<n>118:121</n> <n>(Ain)</n> I have done judgment and justice: * give me not up to them that slander me.
<n>118:122</n> Uphold thy servant unto good: * let not the proud calumniate me.
<n>118:123</n> My eyes have fainted after thy salvation: * and for the word of thy justice.
<n>118:124</n> Deal with thy servant according to thy mercy: * and teach me thy justifications.
<n>118:125</n> I am thy servant: * give me understanding that I may know thy testimonies.
<n>118:126</n> It is time, O Lord, to do: * they have dissipated thy law.
<n>118:127</n> Therefore have I loved thy commandments * above gold and the topaz.
<n>118:128</n> Therefore was I directed to all thy commandments: * I have hated all wicked ways.
11.9422bcdef7:
<n>118:129</n> <n>(Phe)</n> Mirabília testimónia tua: * ídeo scrutáta est ea ánima mea.
<n>118:130</n> Declarátio sermónum tuórum illúminat: * et intelléctum dat párvulis.
<n>118:131</n> Os meum apérui, et attráxi spíritum: * quia mandáta tua desiderábam.
<n>118:132</n> Áspice in me, et miserére mei, * secúndum iudícium diligéntium nomen tuum.
<n>118:133</n> Gressus meos dírige secúndum elóquium tuum: * et non dominétur mei omnis iniustítia.
<n>118:134</n> Rédime me a calúmniis hóminum: * ut custódiam mandáta tua.
<n>118:135</n> Fáciem tuam illúmina super servum tuum: * et doce me iustificatiónes tuas.
<n>118:136</n> Éxitus aquárum deduxérunt óculi mei: * quia non custodiérunt legem tuam.
<n>118:137</n> <n>(Sade)</n> Iustus es, Dómine: * et rectum iudícium tuum.
<n>118:138</n> Mandásti iustítiam testimónia tua: * et veritátem tuam nimis.
<n>118:139</n> Tabéscere me fecit zelus meus: * quia oblíti sunt verba tua inimíci mei.
<n>118:140</n> Ignítum elóquium tuum veheménter: * et servus tuus diléxit illud.
<n>118:141</n> Adolescéntulus sum ego et contémptus: * iustificatiónes tuas non sum oblítus.
<n>118:142</n> Iustítia tua, iustítia in ætérnum: * et lex tua véritas.
<n>118:143</n> Tribulátio, et angústia invenérunt me: * mandáta tua meditátio mea est.
<n>118:144</n> Ǽquitas testimónia tua in ætérnum: * intelléctum da mihi, et vivam.
11.f170de9428:
<n>118:129</n> <n>(Phe)</n> Thy testimonies are wonderful: * therefore my soul hath sought them.
<n>118:130</n> The declaration of thy words giveth light: * and giveth understanding to little ones.
<n>118:131</n> I opened my mouth, and panted: * because I longed for thy commandments.
<n>118:132</n> Look thou upon me, and have mercy on me, * according to the judgment of them that love thy name.
<n>118:133</n> Direct my steps according to thy word: * and let no iniquity have dominion over me.
<n>118:134</n> Redeem me from the calumnies of men: * that I may keep thy commandments.
<n>118:135</n> Make thy face to shine upon thy servant: * and teach me thy justifications.
<n>118:136</n> My eyes have sent forth springs of water: * because they have not kept thy law.
<n>118:137</n> <n>(Sade)</n> Thou art just, O Lord: * and thy judgment is right.
<n>118:138</n> Thou hast commanded justice thy testimonies: * and thy truth exceedingly.
<n>118:139</n> My zeal hath made me pine away: * because my enemies forgot thy words.
<n>118:140</n> Thy word is exceedingly refined: * and thy servant hath loved it.
<n>118:141</n> I am very young and despised; but * I forget not thy justifications.
<n>118:142</n> Thy justice is justice for ever: * and thy law is the truth.
<n>118:143</n> Trouble and anguish have found me: * thy commandments are my meditation.
<n>118:144</n> Thy testimonies are justice for ever: * give me understanding, and I shall live.
11.52d623b4a3:
<n>118:145</n> <n>(Coph)</n> Clamávi in toto corde meo, exáudi me, Dómine: * iustificatiónes tuas requíram.
<n>118:146</n> Clamávi ad te, salvum me fac: * ut custódiam mandáta tua.
<n>118:147</n> Prævéni in maturitáte, et clamávi: * quia in verba tua supersperávi.
<n>118:148</n> Prævenérunt óculi mei ad te dilúculo: * ut meditárer elóquia tua.
<n>118:149</n> Vocem meam audi secúndum misericórdiam tuam, Dómine: * et secúndum iudícium tuum vivífica me.
<n>118:150</n> Appropinquavérunt persequéntes me iniquitáti: * a lege autem tua longe facti sunt.
<n>118:151</n> Prope es tu, Dómine: * et omnes viæ tuæ véritas.
<n>118:152</n> Inítio cognóvi de testimóniis tuis: * quia in ætérnum fundásti ea.
<n>118:153</n> <n>(Res)</n> Vide humilitátem meam, et éripe me: * quia legem tuam non sum oblítus.
<n>118:154</n> Iúdica iudícium meum, et rédime me: * propter elóquium tuum vivífica me.
<n>118:155</n> Longe a peccatóribus salus: * quia iustificatiónes tuas non exquisiérunt.
<n>118:156</n> Misericórdiæ tuæ multæ, Dómine: * secúndum iudícium tuum vivífica me.
<n>118:157</n> Multi qui persequúntur me, et tríbulant me: * a testimóniis tuis non declinávi.
<n>118:158</n> Vidi prævaricántes, et tabescébam: * quia elóquia tua non custodiérunt.
<n>118:159</n> Vide quóniam mandáta tua diléxi, Dómine: * in misericórdia tua vivífica me.
<n>118:160</n> Princípium verbórum tuórum, véritas: * in ætérnum ómnia iudícia iustítiæ tuæ.
11.e39df4bd4a:
<n>118:145</n> <n>(Coph)</n> I cried with my whole heart, hear me, O Lord: * I will seek thy justifications.
<n>118:146</n> I cried unto thee, save me: * that I may keep thy commandments.
<n>118:147</n> I prevented the dawning of the day, and cried: * because in thy words I very much hoped.
<n>118:148</n> My eyes to thee have prevented the morning: * that I might meditate on thy words.
<n>118:149</n> Hear thou my voice, O Lord, according to thy mercy: * and quicken me according to thy judgment.
<n>118:150</n> They that persecute me have drawn nigh to iniquity; * but they are gone far off from thy law.
<n>118:151</n> Thou art near, O Lord: * and all thy ways are truth.
<n>118:152</n> I have known from the beginning concerning thy testimonies: * that thou hast founded them for ever.
<n>118:153</n> <n>(Res)</n> See my humiliation and deliver me: * for I have not forgotten thy law.
<n>118:154</n> Judge my judgment and redeem me: * quicken thou me for thy word’s sake.
<n>118:155</n> Salvation is far from sinners; * because they have not sought thy justifications.
<n>118:156</n> Many, O Lord, are thy mercies: * quicken me according to thy judgment.
<n>118:157</n> Many are they that persecute me, and afflict me; * but I have not declined from thy testimonies.
<n>118:158</n> I beheld the transgressors, and I pined away; * because they kept not thy word.
<n>118:159</n> Behold I have loved thy commandments, O Lord; * quicken me thou in thy mercy.
<n>118:160</n> The beginning of thy words is truth: * all the judgments of thy justice are for ever.
11.b6a448c904:
<n>118:161</n> <n>(Sin)</n> Príncipes persecúti sunt me gratis: * et a verbis tuis formidávit cor meum.
<n>118:162</n> Lætábor ego super elóquia tua: * sicut qui invénit spólia multa.
<n>118:163</n> Iniquitátem ódio hábui, et abominátus sum: * legem autem tuam diléxi.
<n>118:164</n> Sépties in die laudem dixi tibi, * super iudícia iustítiæ tuæ.
<n>118:165</n> Pax multa diligéntibus legem tuam: * et non est illis scándalum.
<n>118:166</n> Exspectábam salutáre tuum, Dómine: * et mandáta tua diléxi.
<n>118:167</n> Custodívit ánima mea testimónia tua: * et diléxit ea veheménter.
<n>118:168</n> Servávi mandáta tua, et testimónia tua: * quia omnes viæ meæ in conspéctu tuo.
<n>118:169</n> <n>(Thau)</n> Appropínquet deprecátio mea in conspéctu tuo, Dómine: * iuxta elóquium tuum da mihi intelléctum.
<n>118:170</n> Intret postulátio mea in conspéctu tuo: * secúndum elóquium tuum éripe me.
<n>118:171</n> Eructábunt lábia mea hymnum, * cum docúeris me iustificatiónes tuas.
<n>118:172</n> Pronuntiábit lingua mea elóquium tuum: * quia ómnia mandáta tua ǽquitas.
<n>118:173</n> Fiat manus tua ut salvet me: * quóniam mandáta tua elégi.
<n>118:174</n> Concupívi salutáre tuum, Dómine: * et lex tua meditátio mea est.
<n>118:175</n> Vivet ánima mea, et laudábit te: * et iudícia tua adiuvábunt me.
<n>118:176</n> Errávi, sicut ovis, quæ périit: * quære servum tuum, quia mandáta tua non sum oblítus.
11.efa4624ea1:
<n>118:161</n> <n>(Sin)</n> Princes have persecuted me without cause: * and my heart hath been in awe of thy words.
<n>118:162</n> I will rejoice at thy words, * as one that hath found great spoil.
<n>118:163</n> I have hated and abhorred iniquity; * but I have loved thy law.
<n>118:164</n> Seven times a day I have given praise to thee, * for the judgments of thy justice.
<n>118:165</n> Much peace have they that love thy law, * and to them there is no stumbling-block.
<n>118:166</n> I looked for thy salvation, O Lord: * and I loved thy commandments.
<n>118:167</n> My soul hath kept thy testimonies: * and hath loved them exceedingly.
<n>118:168</n> I have kept thy commandments and thy testimonies: * because all my ways are in thy sight.
<n>118:169</n> <n>(Tau)</n> Let my supplication, O Lord, come near in thy sight: * give me understanding according to thy word.
<n>118:170</n> Let my request come in before thee; * deliver thou me according to thy word.
<n>118:171</n> My lips shall utter a hymn, * when thou shalt teach me thy justifications.
<n>118:172</n> My tongue shall pronounce thy word: * because all thy commandments are justice.
<n>118:173</n> Let thy hand be with me to save me; * for I have chosen thy precepts.
<n>118:174</n> I have longed for thy salvation, O Lord; * and thy law is my meditation.
<n>118:175</n> My soul shall live and shall praise thee: * and thy judgments shall help me.
<n>118:176</n> I have gone astray like a sheep that is lost: * seek thy servant, because I have not forgotten thy commandments.
11.c4e6608dff:
<n>111:1</n> Beátus vir, qui timet Dóminum: * in mandátis eius volet nimis.
<n>111:2</n> Potens in terra erit semen eius: * generátio rectórum benedicétur.
<n>111:3</n> Glória, et divítiæ in domo eius: * et iustítia eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi.
<n>111:4</n> Exórtum est in ténebris lumen rectis: * miséricors, et miserátor, et iustus.
<n>111:5</n> Iucúndus homo qui miserétur et cómmodat, dispónet sermónes suos in iudício: * quia in ætérnum non commovébitur.
<n>111:7</n> In memória ætérna erit iustus: * ab auditióne mala non timébit.
<n>111:7</n> Parátum cor eius speráre in Dómino, confirmátum est cor eius: * non commovébitur donec despíciat inimícos suos.
<n>111:9</n> Dispérsit, dedit paupéribus: iustítia eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi, * cornu eius exaltábitur in glória.
<n>111:10</n> Peccátor vidébit, et irascétur, déntibus suis fremet et tabéscet: * desidérium peccatórum períbit.
11.665e1166f3:
<n>111:1</n> Blessed is the man that feareth the Lord: * he shall delight exceedingly in his commandments.
<n>111:2</n> His seed shall be mighty upon earth: * the generation of the righteous shall be blessed.
<n>111:3</n> Glory and wealth shall be in his house: * and his justice remaineth for ever and ever.
<n>111:4</n> To the righteous a light is risen up in darkness: * he is merciful, and compassionate and just.
<n>111:5</n> Acceptable is the man that sheweth mercy and lendeth: he shall order his words with judgment: * because he shall not be moved for ever.
<n>111:7</n> The just shall be in everlasting remembrance: * he shall not fear the evil hearing.
<n>111:7</n> His heart is ready to hope in the Lord: his heart is strengthened, * he shall not be moved until he look over his enemies.
<n>111:9</n> He hath distributed, he hath given to the poor: his justice remaineth for ever and ever: * his horn shall be exalted in glory.
<n>111:10</n> The wicked shall see, and shall be angry, he shall gnash with his teeth and pine away: * the desire of the wicked shall perish.
11.dc3358e6e7:
<n>112:1</n> Laudáte, púeri, Dóminum: * laudáte nomen Dómini.
<n>112:2</n> <n>(fit reverentia)</n> Sit nomen Dómini benedíctum, * ex hoc nunc, et usque in sǽculum.
<n>112:3</n> A solis ortu usque ad occásum, * laudábile nomen Dómini.
<n>112:4</n> Excélsus super omnes gentes Dóminus, * et super cælos glória eius.
<n>112:5</n> Quis sicut Dóminus, Deus noster, qui in altis hábitat, * et humília réspicit in cælo et in terra?
<n>112:7</n> Súscitans a terra ínopem, * et de stércore érigens páuperem:
<n>112:8</n> Ut cóllocet eum cum princípibus, * cum princípibus pópuli sui.
<n>112:9</n> Qui habitáre facit stérilem in domo, * matrem filiórum lætántem.
11.0dad385425:
<n>112:1</n> Praise the Lord, ye children: * praise ye the name of the Lord.
<n>112:2</n> <n>(bow head)</n> Blessed be the name of the Lord, * from henceforth now and for ever.
<n>112:3</n> From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same, * the name of the Lord is worthy of praise.
<n>112:4</n> The Lord is high above all nations; * and his glory above the heavens.
<n>112:5</n> Who is as the Lord our God, who dwelleth on high: * and looketh down on the low things in heaven and in earth?
<n>112:7</n> Raising up the needy from the earth, * and lifting up the poor out of the dunghill:
<n>112:8</n> That he may place him with princes, * with the princes of his people.
<n>112:9</n> Who maketh a barren woman to dwell in a house, * the joyful mother of children.
11.67ccb5cc64:
<n>115:1</n> Crédidi, propter quod locútus sum: * ego autem humiliátus sum nimis.
<n>115:2</n> Ego dixi in excéssu meo: * Omnis homo mendax.
<n>115:3</n> Quid retríbuam Dómino, * pro ómnibus, quæ retríbuit mihi?
<n>115:4</n> Cálicem salutáris accípiam: * et nomen Dómini invocábo.
<n>115:5</n> Vota mea Dómino reddam coram omni pópulo eius: * pretiósa in conspéctu Dómini mors sanctórum eius:
<n>115:7</n> O Dómine, quia ego servus tuus: * ego servus tuus, et fílius ancíllæ tuæ.
<n>115:7</n> Dirupísti víncula mea: * tibi sacrificábo hóstiam laudis, et nomen Dómini invocábo.
<n>115:9</n> Vota mea Dómino reddam in conspéctu omnis pópuli eius: * in átriis domus Dómini, in médio tui, Ierúsalem.
11.e89fc8318a:
<n>115:1</n> I have believed, therefore have I spoken; * but I have been humbled exceedingly.
<n>115:2</n> I said in my excess: * Every man is a liar.
<n>115:3</n> What shall I render to the Lord, * for all the things that he hath rendered to me?
<n>115:4</n> I will take the chalice of salvation; * and I will call upon the name of the Lord.
<n>115:5</n> I will pay my vows to the Lord before all his people: * precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints.
<n>115:7</n> O Lord, for I am thy servant: * I am thy servant, and the son of thy handmaid.
<n>115:7</n> Thou hast broken my bonds: * I will sacrifice to thee the sacrifice of praise, and I will call upon the name of the Lord.
<n>115:9</n> I will pay my vows to the Lord in the sight of all his people: * in the courts of the house of the Lord, in the midst of thee, O Jerusalem.
11.063ae82b42:
<n>114:1</n> Diléxi, quóniam exáudiet Dóminus * vocem oratiónis meæ.
<n>114:2</n> Quia inclinávit aurem suam mihi: * et in diébus meis invocábo.
<n>114:3</n> Circumdedérunt me dolóres mortis: * et perícula inférni invenérunt me.
<n>114:3</n> Tribulatiónem et dolórem invéni: * et nomen Dómini invocávi.
<n>114:4</n> O Dómine, líbera ánimam meam: * miséricors Dóminus, et iustus, et Deus noster miserétur.
<n>114:6</n> Custódiens párvulos Dóminus: * humiliátus sum, et liberávit me.
<n>114:7</n> Convértere, ánima mea, in réquiem tuam: * quia Dóminus benefécit tibi.
<n>114:8</n> Quia erípuit ánimam meam de morte: * óculos meos a lácrimis, pedes meos a lapsu.
<n>114:9</n> Placébo Dómino * in regióne vivórum.
11.9d5c292df2:
<n>114:1</n> I have loved, because the Lord will hear * the voice of my prayer.
<n>114:2</n> Because he hath inclined his ear unto me: * and in my days I will call upon him.
<n>114:3</n> The sorrows of death have compassed me: * and the perils of hell have found me.
<n>114:3</n> I met with trouble and sorrow: * and I called upon the name of the Lord.
<n>114:4</n> O Lord, deliver my soul. * The Lord is merciful and just, and our God sheweth mercy.
<n>114:6</n> The Lord is the keeper of little ones: * I was humbled, and he delivered me.
<n>114:7</n> Turn, O my soul, into thy rest: * for the Lord hath been bountiful to thee.
<n>114:8</n> For he hath delivered my soul from death: * my eyes from tears, my feet from falling.
<n>114:9</n> I will please the Lord * in the land of the living.
11.7f05068cbb:
<n>119:1</n> Ad Dóminum cum tribulárer clamávi: * et exaudívit me.
<n>119:2</n> Dómine, líbera ánimam meam a lábiis iníquis, * et a lingua dolósa.
<n>119:3</n> Quid detur tibi, aut quid apponátur tibi * ad linguam dolósam?
<n>119:4</n> Sagíttæ poténtis acútæ, * cum carbónibus desolatóriis.
<n>119:5</n> Heu mihi, quia incolátus meus prolongátus est: habitávi cum habitántibus Cedar: * multum íncola fuit ánima mea.
<n>119:7</n> Cum his, qui odérunt pacem, eram pacíficus: * cum loquébar illis, impugnábant me gratis.
11.44adc1dc53:
<n>119:1</n> In my trouble I cried to the Lord: * and he heard me.
<n>119:2</n> O Lord, deliver my soul from wicked lips, * and a deceitful tongue.
<n>119:3</n> What shall be given to thee, or what shall be added to thee, * to a deceitful tongue?
<n>119:4</n> The sharp arrows of the mighty, * with coals that lay waste.
<n>119:5</n> Woe is me, that my sojourning is prolonged! I have dwelt with the inhabitants of Cedar: * my soul hath been long a sojourner.
<n>119:7</n> With them that hated peace I was peaceable: * when I spoke to them they fought against me without cause.
11.ac8cbdfba3:
<n>117:1</n> Confitémini Dómino quóniam bonus: * quóniam in sǽculum misericórdia eius.
<n>117:2</n> Dicat nunc Israël quóniam bonus: * quóniam in sǽculum misericórdia eius.
<n>117:3</n> Dicat nunc domus Aaron: * quóniam in sǽculum misericórdia eius.
<n>117:4</n> Dicant nunc qui timent Dóminum: * quóniam in sǽculum misericórdia eius.
<n>117:5</n> De tribulatióne invocávi Dóminum: * et exaudívit me in latitúdine Dóminus.
<n>117:6</n> Dóminus mihi adiútor: * non timébo quid fáciat mihi homo.
<n>117:7</n> Dóminus mihi adiútor: * et ego despíciam inimícos meos.
<n>117:8</n> Bonum est confídere in Dómino, * quam confídere in hómine:
<n>117:9</n> Bonum est speráre in Dómino, * quam speráre in princípibus.
<n>117:10</n> Omnes gentes circuiérunt me: * et in nómine Dómini quia ultus sum in eos.
<n>117:11</n> Circumdántes circumdedérunt me: * et in nómine Dómini quia ultus sum in eos.
<n>117:12</n> Circumdedérunt me sicut apes, et exarsérunt sicut ignis in spinis: * et in nómine Dómini quia ultus sum in eos.
<n>117:13</n> Impúlsus evérsus sum ut cáderem: * et Dóminus suscépit me.
<n>117:14</n> Fortitúdo mea, et laus mea Dóminus: * et factus est mihi in salútem.
<n>117:15</n> Vox exsultatiónis, et salútis * in tabernáculis iustórum.
<n>117:16</n> Déxtera Dómini fecit virtútem: déxtera Dómini exaltávit me, * déxtera Dómini fecit virtútem.
<n>117:17</n> Non móriar, sed vivam: * et narrábo ópera Dómini.
<n>117:18</n> Castígans castigávit me Dóminus: * et morti non trádidit me.
<n>117:19</n> Aperíte mihi portas iustítiæ, ingréssus in eas confitébor Dómino: * hæc porta Dómini, iusti intrábunt in eam.
<n>117:21</n> Confitébor tibi quóniam exaudísti me: * et factus es mihi in salútem.
<n>117:22</n> Lápidem, quem reprobavérunt ædificántes: * hic factus est in caput ánguli.
<n>117:23</n> A Dómino factum est istud: * et est mirábile in óculis nostris.
<n>117:24</n> Hæc est dies, quam fecit Dóminus: * exsultémus, et lætémur in ea.
<n>117:25</n> O Dómine, salvum me fac, o Dómine, bene prosperáre: * benedíctus qui venit in nómine Dómini.
<n>117:26</n> Benedíximus vobis de domo Dómini: * Deus Dóminus, et illúxit nobis.
<n>117:27</n> Constitúite diem solémnem in condénsis, * usque ad cornu altáris.
<n>117:28</n> Deus meus es tu, et confitébor tibi: * Deus meus es tu, et exaltábo te.
<n>117:28</n> Confitébor tibi quóniam exaudísti me * et factus es mihi in salútem.
<n>117:29</n> Confitémini Dómino quóniam bonus: * quóniam in sǽculum misericórdia eius.
11.d07743ba10:
<n>117:1</n> Give praise to the Lord, for he is good: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>117:2</n> Let Israel now say, that he is good: * that his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>117:3</n> Let the house of Aaron now say, * that his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>117:4</n> Let them that fear the Lord now say, * that his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>117:5</n> In my trouble I called upon the Lord: * and the Lord heard me, and enlarged me.
<n>117:6</n> The Lord is my helper: * I will not fear what man can do unto me.
<n>117:7</n> The Lord is my helper: * and I will look over my enemies.
<n>117:8</n> It is good to confide in the Lord, * rather than to have confidence in man.
<n>117:9</n> It is good to trust in the Lord, * rather than to trust in princes.
<n>117:10</n> All nations compassed me about; * and in the name of the Lord I have been revenged on them.
<n>117:11</n> Surrounding me they compassed me about: * and in the name of the Lord I have been revenged on them.
<n>117:12</n> They surrounded me like bees, and they burned like fire among thorns: * and in the name of the Lord I was revenged on them.
<n>117:13</n> Being pushed I was overturned that I might fall: * but the Lord supported me.
<n>117:14</n> The Lord is my strength and my praise: * and he is become my salvation.
<n>117:15</n> The voice of rejoicing and of salvation * is in the tabernacles of the just.
<n>117:16</n> The right hand of the Lord hath wrought strength: the right hand of the Lord hath exalted me: * the right hand of the Lord hath wrought strength.
<n>117:17</n> I shall not die, but live: * and shall declare the works of the Lord.
<n>117:18</n> The Lord chastising hath chastised me: * but he hath not delivered me over to death.
<n>117:19</n> Open ye to me the gates of justice: I will go in to them, and give praise to the Lord. * This is the gate of the Lord, the just shall enter into it.
<n>117:21</n> I will give glory to thee because thou hast heard me: * and art become my salvation.
<n>117:22</n> The stone which the builders rejected; * the same is become the head of the corner.
<n>117:23</n> This is the Lord’s doing: * and it is wonderful in our eyes.
<n>117:24</n> This is the day which the Lord hath made: * let us be glad and rejoice therein.
<n>117:25</n> O Lord, save me: O Lord, give good success: * Blessed be he that cometh in the name of the Lord.
<n>117:26</n> We have blessed you out of the house of the Lord: * The Lord is God, and he hath shone upon us.
<n>117:27</n> Appoint a solemn day, with shady boughs, * even to the horn of the altar.
<n>117:28</n> Thou art my God, and I will praise thee: * thou art my God, and I will exalt thee.
<n>117:28</n> I will praise thee, because thou hast heard me, * and art become my salvation.
<n>117:29</n> O praise ye the Lord, for he is good: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
11.f90ddf5594:
<n>110:1</n> Confitébor tibi, Dómine, in toto corde meo: * in consílio iustórum, et congregatióne.
<n>110:2</n> Magna ópera Dómini: * exquisíta in omnes voluntátes eius.
<n>110:3</n> Conféssio et magnificéntia opus eius: * et iustítia eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi.
<n>110:4</n> Memóriam fecit mirabílium suórum, miséricors et miserátor Dóminus: * escam dedit timéntibus se.
<n>110:5</n> Memor erit in sǽculum testaménti sui: * virtútem óperum suórum annuntiábit pópulo suo:
<n>110:7</n> Ut det illis hereditátem géntium: * ópera mánuum eius véritas, et iudícium.
<n>110:8</n> Fidélia ómnia mandáta eius: confirmáta in sǽculum sǽculi, * facta in veritáte et æquitáte.
<n>110:9</n> Redemptiónem misit pópulo suo: * mandávit in ætérnum testaméntum suum.
<n>110:9</n> <n>(fit reverentia)</n> Sanctum, et terríbile nomen eius: * inítium sapiéntiæ timor Dómini.
<n>110:10</n> Intelléctus bonus ómnibus faciéntibus eum: * laudátio eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi.
11.359551b4c9:
<n>110:1</n> I will praise thee, O Lord, with my whole heart; * in the council of the just, and in the congregation.
<n>110:2</n> Great are the works of the Lord: * sought out according to all his wills.
<n>110:3</n> His work is praise and magnificence: * and his justice continueth for ever and ever.
<n>110:4</n> He hath made a remembrance of his wonderful works, being a merciful and gracious Lord: * he hath given food to them that fear him.
<n>110:5</n> He will be mindful for ever of his covenant: * he will shew forth to his people the power of his works.
<n>110:7</n> That he may give them the inheritance of the Gentiles: * the works of his hands are truth and judgment.
<n>110:8</n> All his commandments are faithful: confirmed for ever and ever, * made in truth and equity.
<n>110:9</n> He hath sent redemption to his people: * he hath commanded his covenant for ever.
<n>110:9</n> <n>(bow head)</n> Holy and terrible is his name: * the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.
<n>110:10</n> A good understanding to all that do it: * his praise continueth for ever and ever.
11.1ff9239bb6:
<n>113:1</n> In éxitu Israël de Ægýpto, * domus Iacob de pópulo bárbaro:
<n>113:2</n> Facta est Iudǽa sanctificátio eius, * Israël potéstas eius.
<n>113:3</n> Mare vidit, et fugit: * Iordánis convérsus est retrórsum.
<n>113:4</n> Montes exsultavérunt ut aríetes, * et colles sicut agni óvium.
<n>113:5</n> Quid est tibi, mare, quod fugísti: * et tu, Iordánis, quia convérsus es retrórsum?
<n>113:6</n> Montes, exsultástis sicut aríetes, * et colles, sicut agni óvium.
<n>113:7</n> A fácie Dómini mota est terra, * a fácie Dei Iacob.
<n>113:8</n> Qui convértit petram in stagna aquárum, * et rupem in fontes aquárum.
<n>113:9</n> Non nobis, Dómine, non nobis: * sed nómini tuo da glóriam.
<n>113:10</n> Super misericórdia tua, et veritáte tua: * nequándo dicant gentes: Ubi est Deus eórum?
<n>113:11</n> Deus autem noster in cælo: * ómnia quæcúmque vóluit, fecit.
<n>113:12</n> Simulácra géntium argéntum, et aurum, * ópera mánuum hóminum.
<n>113:13</n> Os habent, et non loquéntur: * óculos habent, et non vidébunt.
<n>113:14</n> Aures habent, et non áudient: * nares habent, et non odorábunt.
<n>113:15</n> Manus habent, et non palpábunt: pedes habent, et non ambulábunt: * non clamábunt in gútture suo.
<n>113:16</n> Símiles illis fiant qui fáciunt ea: * et omnes qui confídunt in eis.
<n>113:17</n> Domus Israël sperávit in Dómino: * adiútor eórum et protéctor eórum est,
<n>113:18</n> Domus Aaron sperávit in Dómino: * adiútor eórum et protéctor eórum est,
<n>113:19</n> Qui timent Dóminum, speravérunt in Dómino: * adiútor eórum et protéctor eórum est.
<n>113:20</n> Dóminus memor fuit nostri: * et benedíxit nobis:
<n>113:20</n> Benedíxit dómui Israël: * benedíxit dómui Aaron.
<n>113:21</n> Benedíxit ómnibus, qui timent Dóminum, * pusíllis cum maióribus.
<n>113:22</n> Adíciat Dóminus super vos: * super vos, et super fílios vestros.
<n>113:23</n> Benedícti vos a Dómino, * qui fecit cælum, et terram.
<n>113:24</n> Cælum cæli Dómino: * terram autem dedit fíliis hóminum.
<n>113:25</n> Non mórtui laudábunt te, Dómine: * neque omnes, qui descéndunt in inférnum.
<n>113:26</n> Sed nos qui vívimus, benedícimus Dómino, * ex hoc nunc et usque in sǽculum.
11.8d851750b7:
<n>113:1</n> When Israel went out of Egypt, * the house of Jacob from a barbarous people:
<n>113:2</n> Judea was made his sanctuary, * Israel his dominion.
<n>113:3</n> The sea saw and fled: * Jordan was turned back.
<n>113:4</n> The mountains skipped like rams, * and the hills like the lambs of the flock.
<n>113:5</n> What ailed thee, O thou sea, that thou didst flee: * and thou, O Jordan, that thou wast turned back?
<n>113:6</n> Ye mountains, that ye skipped like rams, * and ye hills, like lambs of the flock?
<n>113:7</n> At the presence of the Lord the earth was moved, * at the presence of the God of Jacob:
<n>113:8</n> Who turned the rock into pools of water, * and the stony hill into fountains of waters.
<n>113:9</n> Not to us, O Lord, not to us; * but to thy name give glory.
<n>113:10</n> For thy mercy, and for thy truth’s sake: * lest the Gentiles should say: Where is their God?
<n>113:11</n> But our God is in heaven: * he hath done all things whatsoever he would.
<n>113:12</n> The idols of the Gentiles are silver and gold, * the works of the hands of men.
<n>113:13</n> They have mouths and speak not: * they have eyes and see not.
<n>113:14</n> They have ears and hear not: * they have noses and smell not.
<n>113:15</n> They have hands and feel not: they have feet and walk not: * neither shall they cry out through their throat.
<n>113:16</n> Let them that make them become like unto them: * and all such as trust in them.
<n>113:17</n> The house of Israel hath hoped in the Lord: * he is their helper and their protector.
<n>113:18</n> The house of Aaron hath hoped in the Lord: * he is their helper and their protector.
<n>113:19</n> They that fear the Lord have hoped in the Lord: * he is their helper and their protector.
<n>113:20</n> The Lord hath been mindful of us, * and hath blessed us.
<n>113:20</n> He hath blessed the house of Israel: * he hath blessed the house of Aaron.
<n>113:21</n> He hath blessed all that fear the Lord, * both little and great.
<n>113:22</n> May the Lord add blessings upon you: * upon you, and upon your children.
<n>113:23</n> Blessed be you of the Lord, * who made heaven and earth.
<n>113:24</n> The heaven of heaven is the Lord’s: * but the earth he has given to the children of men.
<n>113:25</n> The dead shall not praise thee, O Lord: * nor any of them that go down to hell.
<n>113:26</n> But we that live bless the Lord: * from this time now and for ever.
